ব্যাংক নিয়োগ প্রস্তুতি.question: ১) If the probability of rain on any given day in City Rangpur is 50 percent, what is the probability that it rains on exactly 2 days in a 4-day period?
ব্যাংক নিয়োগ প্রস্তুতি.exp:
Question: If the probability of rain on any given day in City Rangpur is 50 percent, what is the probability that it rains on exactly 2 days in a 4-day period?

Solution:
If the probability of rain on any given day in City Rangpur is 50 percent
the probability of rain on any given day = 1/2
the probability of no rain on any given day = 1/2

selecting 2 days out of 4 = 4C2

∴the probability that it rains on exactly 3 days in a 5-day period is = 4C2 × (1/2) × (1/2) × 1/2 × 1/2
= 6 × 1/24
= 6 × 1/16
= 3/8

ব্যাংক নিয়োগ প্রস্তুতি.question: ৪) <sup>6</sup>P<sub>m</sub> = 360, <sup>6</sup>C<sub>m</sub> = 15, what is the value of m?

Question: 6Pm = 360, 6Cm = 15, what is the value of m?

Solution:
6Pm = 360
⇒ 6!/(6 - m)! = 360........(1)

6Cm = 15
⇒ 6!/m! (6 - m)! = 15..........(2)

(1) ÷ (2) ,
{6!/(6 - m)!} / {6!/m! (6 - m)! } = 360/15
⇒ m! = 24
= 4 × 3 × 2 × 1

∴ m = 4

ব্যাংক নিয়োগ প্রস্তুতি.question: ৫) A bag contains 4 red and 6 black balls. A ball is drawn at random from the bag, its colour is observed and this ball along with two additional balls of the same colour are returned to the bag. If now a ball is drawn at random from the bag, then the probability that this drawn ball is red is :
ব্যাংক নিয়োগ প্রস্তুতি.exp:
Question: A bag contains 4 red and 6 black balls. A ball is drawn at random from the bag, its colour is observed and this ball along with two additional balls of the same colour are returned to the bag. If now a ball is drawn at random from the bag, then the probability that this drawn ball is red is :

Solution: 
There are 2 possible cases: the first ball drawn is red or black.
P(first ball black) = 6/10
P(first ball red) = 4/10

P(second ball red | first ball drawn is black) = 4/12
P(second ball red | first ball drawn is red) = 6/12 = 1/2

The probability of the second ball being red, P(R) = (4/10)×(1/2) + (6/10) ×(4/12)
= (1/5) + (1/5)
= 2/5

Question: In a survey among the readers of newspapers, it was found that 65 persons read the Prothom Alo, 40 persons read the Bhorer Kagoj, 45 read the Janakantho, 52 read the Jugantor. If one person is chosen at random from there readers, what is the probability that the person doesn't read the Jugantor? 

Solution:
Total persons = 65 + 40 + 45 + 52
= 202

probability of that person reading jugantor = 52/202
= 26/101

the probability that the person doesn't read the Jugantor = 1 - 26/101
= (101 - 26)/101
= 75/101

Solution:
ways to choose 5 from part A = 10C5
ways to choose 8 from part B = 10C8

choose 5 from part A and 8 from part B = 10C5 × 10C8

Question: In how many ways can 5 examination papers be arranged so that the best and the worst papers never come together?

Solution:
Total ways = 5!
= 120 ways

if two papers come together, we can consider them one.
ways that they will come together = 4! × 2!
= 24 × 2
= 48 ways

∴ ways the best and the worst papers never come together = 120 - 48 ways
= 72 ways

Solution:
Total number of balls = 2 + 3 + 4 
= 9 balls

choosing 3 balls from 9 balls = 9C3
= 84 ways

choosing three balls from black and red balls = 7C3
= 35 ways 

∴ ways can 3 balls be drawn from the box, if at least one white ball is to be included in the draw is = 84 - 35 ways
= 49 ways
